text:
Sean Gallagher: need to lock SLOs + alerting for cost-model-api before we open the flag wider. question: what’s the dependency criticality for Console pages? (breakdown page vs overall console)

Priya Natarajan: cost-model-service is read-path only for Console rn. no hard dependency for navigation/dashboard, only the cost breakdown view + tooltips. Console should degrade to cached/“unavailable” state.

Dylan Brooks: yup. if SCM is down, we can hide the breakdown card and show “Estimated cost temporarily unavailable” + last-known cached (if <24h). rest of Console should not be impacted.

Chloe Martin: +1. backend client will have a tight timeout and fallback to cached. we should not page on a single tenant failing.

Sean Gallagher: ok so not “page-down” critical, but it’s still a key surface for enterprise. proposing SLOs per endpoint tier:
- /v1/cost-model/estimate: 99.9% monthly availability, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 800ms (regional)
- /v1/cost-model/explain: 99.5% monthly availability, p95 < 400ms, p99 < 1200ms
Thoughts?

Neha Kapoor: 99.9 for estimate seems fine if we’re serious about Optimize pipeline dependency too. explain being looser makes sense.

Jordan Lee: determinism/validation can cause 4xx spikes if inputs missing. we should be explicit what counts in SLO (5xx + timeouts) vs client errors.

Allison Grant: pls define “success” as HTTP 2xx/3xx only; exclude 4xx from availability but DO alert on 4xx rate if it regresses (could indicate schema mismatch / rollout bug). also separate out 429 throttles.

Sean Gallagher: agree. SLO availability = (total requests - 5xx - timeouts) / total. 4xx excluded. But we’ll have a “bad request” KPI.

Rafael Mendes: alerting suggestion:
1) availability burn (multi-window): 2%/1h + 5%/6h for estimate; slightly looser for explain
2) latency: p95 + p99 thresholds, but avoid paging on p99 alone unless sustained
3) error: 5xx > 1% for 10m (page), 0.2% for 30m (ticket)
4) mismatch detector (estimated vs metered) = not page, but high sev ticket + canary alert

Grafana Bot: Rafael Mendes shared a dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/scm-service/overview

Talia Benson: can we capture rationale in the SLO doc: Console page is tier-2 dependency (degrades gracefully) but Optimize sweeps may treat estimate as tier-1 for internal workloads.

Neha Kapoor: yeah, also note the mitigation: client-side caching + feature flag. we should include recommended client timeout/retry policy in runbook.

Chloe Martin: current plan for Console client:
- timeout 350ms (estimate) / 600ms (explain)
- 1 retry max w/ jitter only on network errors
- cache TTL 15m for estimate results keyed by (tenant, route, model, region, quant_profile_id, batch/cache config)
If we see timeouts, we’ll stop retries.

Sean Gallagher: one more: do we page when Console starts timing out due to SCM? that’s technically upstream but user-visible.

Dylan Brooks: Console will set circuit breaker. if SCM p95 > 500ms for 5m, we trip breaker and serve cached/empty state. so Console shouldn’t cascade.

Allison Grant: pls add an alert for “circuit breaker open rate” (from Console metrics) but as ticket, not page. paging should be on SCM health itself.

Rafael Mendes: +1. also cardinality: alerts should be global + per-region, NOT per-tenant. per-tenant issues -> support queue.

Sean Gallagher: ok final proposal (for estimate):
- SLO: 99.9% monthly availability
- Latency objective: p95 <= 200ms (regional), p99 <= 800ms
- Paging alerts:
  - 5xx+timeout burn: 2% budget in 1h OR 5% in 6h
  - error rate (5xx+timeout) > 1% for 10m
  - p95 > 350ms for 15m (page during business hours?)
Non-paging:
  - 4xx rate > 3% for 15m (ticket)
  - 429 rate > 1% for 15m (ticket)
  - Console circuit breaker open > 10% of SCM calls for 15m (ticket)
Explain endpoint uses same structure but thresholds + SLO relaxed.

Priya Natarajan: looks good. p95 page during biz hours is fine; off hours make it ticket unless paired w/ elevated 5xx. we don’t want noisy pages from transient load.

Neha Kapoor: +1. also add saturation alert on CPU/mem for the service pods and cache hit ratio dropping (could spike latency).

Rafael Mendes: can wire those as warning panels + tickets first. paging only if it correlates with SLO burn.

Sean Gallagher: cool. i’ll update the cost-model-api-slos doc w/ tiering + rationale and link the dashboard + runbook. Priya/Dylan can you sanity check once posted?

Dylan Brooks: yep.

Priya Natarajan: :thumbsup:
